A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConPress research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C support comparison; content remains matchable despite pagination and table-number changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original self-compression experiments, ConPress benchmark results, ablations, reasoning-behavior analyses and appendix experiments across datasets and models.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds direct test-time compression comparisons in Table 3 and pipeline cost statistics.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains multi-question sampling, correctness filtering and single-question supervised fine-tuning with the same objective. The new cost paragraph documents shortest-correct trace selection without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated tasks remain unchanged, including the mathematical benchmarks, MMLU-STEM and Appendix A's scientific, coding and mixed-domain settings. New Table 3 uses the already covered MATH500 and GSM8K tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds MQ-N2, MQ-N3 and NoThinking as direct comparators to ConPress on R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. Multi-question prompting was previously studied as a phenomenon, but this comparison is new. Table 2's existing comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The added comparison evaluates direct packing of two or three test questions and suppression of explicit reasoning through an empty thinking prefix. These extend the comparative evaluation design; existing training budgets, metrics and Appendix B evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Section 4.2 comparison tests whether direct inference-time compression can substitute for learning compressed behavior. It provides additional diagnostic evidence for the transfer step. Existing question-count and position ablations, difficulty analyses, distribution-shift experiments and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight samples per multi-question prompt in Appendix B.1 and Avg@8 evaluation for AIME25 and AMC. There are no added seed disclosures, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports average accuracy changes and token reductions of -29.9 points/38.3% for MQ-N2, -31.3 points/44.3% for MQ-N3 and -7.7 points/72.5% for NoThinking. Its ConPress results reuse v1's +0.9 points and 45.0% reduction. Existing benchmark and appendix results retain their values; generation-yield and compute-cost statistics are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The definitions of reasoning length, compression rate and reasoning efficiency, together with the supervised fine-tuning objective, are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying self-compression and transferring it through lightweight supervised fine-tuning to reduce reasoning tokens while retaining competitive accuracy. The added comparisons support these existing claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 Section 4.2 adds the interpretation that compression is more reliable when transferred into single-question behavior through training, because the tested inference-time shortcuts sacrifice accuracy. Existing explanations of contextual pressure, difficulty-dependent compression and reasoning behavior remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the 7B pipeline: approximately 24k rollouts/231M tokens, 51k parsed candidates with 84.9% correctness, shortest-correct selection yielding 8k examples/11M tokens, and 84 A100 GPU hours. It also clarifies that both DPO preference candidates are correct responses. These disclosures supplement the retained Appendix B implementation details.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. GPQA changes from its conference citation to the preprint citation of the same work; this is bibliographic metadata, not a new research relationship.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized cost and comparison paragraphs and an Impact Statement, clarifies DPO wording, and corrects grammar and typographical errors. Author affiliations and the publication footer change, while the overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3 and renumbers subsequent tables. Existing ablation tables and Figure 4 move as the text reflows, and the stage-wise table changes the label AMC23 to AMC without changing its values. Existing figure designs and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 3 strengthens the empirical rationale for training ConPress by testing simple inference-time alternatives. The new cost accounting and selection details make the lightweight-training claim easier to assess and improve reproducibility. These are useful, localized gains involving one model and two existing benchmarks; the main results, method and appendix evidence remain unchanged.
